about.summary_education: Computer science at UTM, specialising in network and security. Where the fundamentals came from.
letter: I have spent the last seven years building software for other people's businesses. News portals with millions of readers, an AI voice platform used inside a bank, design systems, mobile apps. Somewhere in there I noticed the work I liked most was the smaller kind: sitting with an owner, understanding how they actually run things, then building the system that holds it.

That is what twlworks is. One person, working directly with the people who will use what I build. No account manager in between, no team to brief, no handover to a stranger. You talk to the person writing the code.

Most of my clients are not tech companies. They grade trading cards, run restaurants, manage property. The operations are real; the tools are spreadsheets, WhatsApp threads and three systems that do not talk to each other. I build the thing that replaces all of it.

I still hold a full-time engineering role, so I take on a small number of projects at a time and I am straight about timelines. It also means I am not desperate for the work — if a project is not right for you, you will hear that from me first.

principles.title: Understand before building
principles.body: Every project starts with a paid audit. If the honest answer is that you do not need custom software, that is a valid outcome and I will say so.

principles.title: One person, start to finish
principles.body: The person you brief is the person who designs it, writes it, ships it and fixes it when something breaks at 11pm.

principles.title: Built to be handed over
principles.body: Your system, your accounts, your code, documented. No lock-in, no hostage situation if you ever want to move on.

principles.title: Fewer projects, properly finished
principles.body: Two or three at a time. Nothing gets parked halfway while I chase the next thing.
